chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by al-Himyari, from Ahmad bin Muhammad, from Uthman bin Isa, from Sama'a bin Mahran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who rejects perfume. He said: He should not reject generosity.

key_terms.طِيب: Perfume or fragrance, used here as a metaphor for a gift or favor.
key_terms.كَرَامَة: Generosity, nobility, or benevolence; referring to the act of giving or the quality of being generous.

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to reject generosity according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the etiquette of receiving gifts by distinguishing between the physical item and the social honor it conveys. He teaches that while one may politely decline the specific object (such as perfume due to personal preference or need, one must never reject the 'karamah' (dignity/respect) of the giver. This principle underscores the Shia emphasis on preserving social bonds and acknowledging the goodwill behind charitable acts, even if the material gift itself is not retained.
